nodes.summary: wiki page 'Reuse distance', 95 lines

nodes.name: reuse distance
nodes.summary: Backward reuse distance R: the number of distinct objects touched since the last access to the same key. A cache of capacity C holds the last C distinct objects, so a request hits exactly when R < C.

nodes.name: mrc curve
nodes.summary: Miss-ratio curve m(C) = P(R >= C), the fraction of requests that miss in a fully associative LRU cache of capacity C.

nodes.name: discrete hazard
nodes.summary: Discrete-time survival model: the binned reuse distance is a survival time, each request contributes one row per bin it was at risk in, and the miss ratio follows from the survival function. Right censoring enters through the risk set, not a discarded row.

nodes.name: risk set expansion
nodes.summary: One training row per (request, bin at risk), label 1 only in the bin where the reuse event happened. The expansion is what makes censored requests usable and is the dominant cost of the fit.

nodes.name: censoring
nodes.summary: A request whose next access has not happened by the end of the observation window is right-censored: it survived past that bin and contributes no event.

nodes.name: kaplan meier floor
nodes.summary: Kaplan-Meier on the binned reuse distance without covariates. The floor the covariates must beat, not a strawman: censoring is handled correctly.

nodes.name: hitcount baseline
nodes.summary: The practitioner's shortcut: regress log(1+frequency), then convert the predicted frequency to a reuse-distance proxy through training deciles. Frequency is not a distance, so the conversion is a marginal and loses to the covariate-free floor.

nodes.name: single row oracle
nodes.summary: A baseline that reads eval_rtilde for the block it scores, so its own bin decides the hit and the curve reconstructs the truth. It reports MAE 0.000000 by construction and is an oracle, not a competitor.

nodes.name: out of time
nodes.summary: Train on the first 60% of a trace, score every 5M-request window of the last 25%. Distribution and grid fixed, only time moves, so drift is isolated.

nodes.name: leave one cluster out
nodes.summary: Train on three traces, score the fourth. The new-cluster test. Confounds model transfer with distribution shift, which is why it is reported beside out-of-time and never alone.

nodes.name: retrain curve
nodes.summary: Test error against training volume with hyper-parameters frozen, so the data axis is not confounded with the search. Answers how much local data a new trace needs.

nodes.name: block bootstrap interval
nodes.summary: Confidence interval for a per-window mean, resampling contiguous blocks of requests rather than single requests, because requests inside a window are autocorrelated and an i.i.d. bootstrap reports an interval that is too narrow.

nodes.name: stale window invalidation
nodes.summary: A per-window score file older than model.json describes a model that no longer exists. Reusing it reports one model's numbers under another model's parameters, so the scorer rescoring is keyed on mtime.

nodes.name: optuna startup phase
nodes.summary: Seeded TPE spends its first 10 trials on random draws, so a study stopped at 12 trials reports capacity ordering rather than a search: three traces returned identical parameters and a Spearman correlation of 1.000. Report a study only past trial 20.

nodes.name: oot protocol
nodes.summary: Windows are 5,000,000 contiguous requests; the split is [0.60, 0.75] in request-index space, so train is the first 60%, validation the next 15%, test the last 25%; the booster is frozen before any test window opens and every window is scored into its own JSON file.
